subject: Map + acceptance checklist for AWS Private Offer — procurement gating items
messages:
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Daniel Perez <daniel.perez@echelonhealth.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, camila_reyes@redwood.com
Date: 2025-05-12T09:12:00Z
Subject: MAP + acceptance checklist for AWS Private Offer — procurement gating items

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I pulled together a concise mutual action plan (attached) that maps technical acceptance gates to procurement milestones and the AWS Private Offer flow. High level:

- Week 0 (today): Redwood provides MAP + termsheet draft and the acceptance criteria workbook (attached).
- Week 1–2: Technical evaluation (staging keys, test queries, performance snapshot).
- Week 3: Security questionnaire closure and final SOC2 evidence handoff.
- Week 4: PO issuance via AWS Private Offer; Redwood issues invoice to AWS marketplace billing (per agreed invoice routing).

A few asks for the Echelon team so we can land the timeline:
1) Confirm primary procurement contact for PO sign and billing routing (procurement@?).
2) Confirm whether Echelon requires an escrow/PO template or will accept Redwood's PO terms submitted to AWS Private Offer.
3) Provide a short list (3) of acceptance test prompts and single-scenario SLA target for latency so we can generate an acceptance report.

I've attached a one-sheet MAP and a draft termsheet. Grace and Camila will coordinate on the technical acceptance runbook. If this looks good, can we lock the kickoff for next Tuesday 5/20?

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Echelon_MAP_v1.xlsx (xlsx), Redwood_PrivateOffer_Termsheet_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: Daniel Perez <daniel.perez@echelonhealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@echelonhealth.com>, Echelon Procurement <procurement@echelonhealth.com>
Date: 2025-05-12T13:04:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP + acceptance checklist for AWS Private Offer — procurement gating items

Jonas —

Appreciate the clean plan and the attachments. Quick answers:

1) Procurement contact: procurement@echelonhealth.com (they'll handle the PO).
2) We prefer the PO go through an AWS Private Offer — we have an internal template but can accept Redwood's terms if the PO lines up with our invoice-to and tax fields. Procurement will send the template this afternoon.
3) Acceptance prompts: we will send 3 representative prompt sets (clinical summarization, de-identification, latency-sensitive triage). SLA target: p95 inference < 400ms on 1024 tokens for the triage scenario.

Two constraints to flag from our side:
- Finance requires invoices to be issued to Echelon via AWS marketplace billing and then reconciled on our monthly statement (we can't accept direct invoices to our AP team).
- Legal needs to confirm data residency notes; we will surface that in the security questionnaire.

Kickoff Tuesday 5/20 works for us — please share the calendar invite.

Thanks,
Daniel
Principal Product Manager
Echelon Health
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, camila_reyes@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2025-05-13T10:18:00Z
Subject: RE: MAP + acceptance checklist for AWS Private Offer — procurement gating items

Folks —

Copying a short internal plan to prepare for Echelon's asks:
- Camila: prep staging keys + quick perf run for their triage prompt (p95 target 400ms at 1k tokens). Capture token counts and GPU type used.
- Karthik: pull the marketplace billing flow doc and confirm that when Echelon accepts a Private Offer, Redwood invoices via AWS and the marketplace posts to Echelon's monthly statement (outline any required metadata fields).
- I'll own SOC2 evidence handoff and the security questionnaire turnaround (aiming 3 business days once we receive their completed form).

Also: legal asked whether we should pre-populate the PO with Redwood's remit address and Redwood's AWS Marketplace Seller ID. If yes, I'll add that to the MAP and the termsheet.

Grace
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: procurement@echelonhealth.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@echelonhealth.com>
Date: 2025-05-14T16:32:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP + acceptance checklist for AWS Private Offer — procurement gating items

Hi Jonas / Grace —

Procurement attached our PO template and a short checklist of onboarding fields we require for AWS Private Offers:
- Billing contact name/email
- Contract start/end dates
- Purchase order number format (ECH-YYYY-####)
- Invoice remittance instructions — must point to AWS marketplace billing with Echelon's vendor code for reconciliation

We confirm we will not accept direct vendor invoices to AP — AWS marketplace billing only. If Redwood needs to provide an SSA or W-9 equivalent, please indicate in the MAP.

We'll also need a confirmation from Redwood specifying the acceptance criteria and smoke-test dates before PO issuance.

Best,
Echelon Procurement Team
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Daniel Perez <daniel.perez@echelonhealth.com>, procurement@echelonhealth.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, camila_reyes@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2025-05-16T15:03:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP + acceptance checklist for AWS Private Offer — procurement gating items

Thanks for the template — that's helpful. Quick next steps and commitments from Redwood:

- We will pre-populate the PO fields with our AWS Seller ID and remit address and return the completed draft by EOD Monday (5/19).
- Camila will run the triage prompt perf snapshot on our staging pool and publish the acceptance report by 5/19 (includes p95 numbers, test corpus, and GPU instance details).
- Grace will deliver the SOC2 evidence packet and our completed security questionnaire by 5/21.
- Once acceptance report and procurement template are aligned, Echelon to issue PO via AWS Private Offer (target 5/23).

I'll share a short kickoff invite for 5/20 to align technical owners, procurement, and finance. If anything blocks these dates from your side, flag now and we'll adapt.

Cheers,
Jonas
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
